storage: volume JSONL <archive>/aircraft_tracked/<HEX>/YYYY-MM.jsonl(.gz): one directory per aircraft (ICAO hex, upper case), one file per UTC month of the fix's own time; a month is gzipped an hour after it ends. Retention: permanent, capped: 50 MiB per plane, 500 MiB total, oldest month first (the current month is never deleted; a plane whose current month alone is at the cap stops being written until the month turns). Not in the R2 cold tier, not rolled up, no age limit.
written_by: server/trackedPlaneLog.ts TrackedPlaneLog.ingest (subscribed to the in-process fix bus, server/aircraftFixBus.ts): every position fix any path receives for a tail on the server's tracked list (server/trackedPlanes.ts, at most 20 tails), written once, never thinned
source: the same community ADS-B providers as the aircraft stream, per row: adsb.lol (ODbL 1.0; the tracked poller's first source and the primary of every other path) + adsb.fi (non-commercial; the tracked poller's second source since 2026-11-19, server/trackedBackup.ts, and a fallback of the other paths) + airplanes.live (non-commercial fallback) + OpenSky Network (non-commercial, only with credentials)
license: per row, by its pv field: adsblol = ODbL 1.0 (commercial use with attribution and share-alike); adsbfi / airplaneslive / opensky = personal / non-commercial only. Rows keep the provider that served them, so the ODbL subset is one filter. Monetization tripwire applies.

field_map.t: unix sec UTC: the fix's OWN time (provider clock minus position age) when ft=1; our receive time when ft is absent (the row carried no position age)
field_map.i: icao24 hex, lower case (entity key; the directory name is the same hex in upper case)
field_map.al: altitude m: barometric (pressure altitude) when the aircraft sent one, else geometric; ak says which
field_map.v: ground speed m/s, rounded (omitted when unknown)
field_map.h: track over ground deg (not the nose heading)
field_map.rg: registration / tail number as the feed gave it
field_map.integrity block: ni np nv si st rc gv sd nb av pt ml tb kla klo kb sp pv, as in the aircraft stream (decode table in server/datacoreArchive.ts aircraftIntegrityFields; sp = position age s at receive; pv = the provider that served the row)
field_map.ag: geometric (GNSS) altitude m above the WGS84 ellipsoid, when broadcast
field_map.vr: broadcast vertical rate m/s (0.1, + climbing), when broadcast
field_map.vs: which rate vr is: b barometric, g geometric; omitted when not told
field_map.ak: which altitude al is: b barometric, g geometric
field_map.ft: 1 = t is the fix's own time; omitted = receive time

confidence_model: RAW: each line is one position fix as a provider served it; no inference, no thinning, no interpolation. The same line format as the aircraft stream's own-time lines (server/datacoreArchive.ts aircraftFixLine), with no x block: geometric altitude and vertical rate are in the flat ag / vr keys, roll is not recorded. A fix is written once: skipped when it is not at least 1 s newer than the last one written for that aircraft, older than 10 minutes, or dated more than 60 s ahead of our clock. The same physical fix can still appear twice, 1 to 2 s apart, when two paths stamp it with different clocks; readers collapse those (server/aircraftTrackData.ts cleanFixes). NOT in this log: the provider's day trace that the tracked poller backfills into the aircraft stream every 15 minutes, and anything from before the tail was tracked. Lines skipped for a cap, low disk, the kill switch or a write error are counted on GET /api/data/aircraft/tracked (log).
cadence: fixes as they occur: every fix received while a tracked tail is broadcasting (about one every 10 s from the tracked poller's adsb.fi loop; more when adsb.lol's daily quota allows its own 5 s ticks or a viewer has the aircraft selected); nothing while it is parked and silent
_note: Universal archive envelope (approved 2026-07-04). Owner's instruction 2026-11-17: the bulk log of every aircraft is off (GLOBAL_SWEEP_ARCHIVE unset), tracked tails keep a full permanent log, and that log is capped. Caps: TRACKED_PLANE_LOG_MAX_MB_PER_PLANE (50), TRACKED_PLANE_LOG_MAX_MB_TOTAL (500). Kill switch: TRACKED_PLANE_LOG=0 (reads still work). Removing a tail from the tracked list keeps its log; it still counts toward the total cap. Read by GET /api/data/aircraft/track/:hex and /fleet for what is older than the local hour files.
